title: introduce-tenant-jitter-batcher-and-adaptive-quant-scaler-with-safety-budgets
author: Maya K. Alvarez
description: Motivation: Some tenants experience oscillating latency/cost patterns when competing for shared batching windows; static batch shapes plus coarse quantization tiers cause either wasted GPU cycles or degraded P75 latency. This PR introduces a tenant-aware 'jittered' batching policy that spreads micro-batch alignment to reduce hot-spot bursts, and pairs it with an adaptive quantization scaler that nudges model quant levels per-tenant within a safety budget to keep unit-econ targets without violating latency SLOs. Scope: server/runtime patch (batch scheduler), policy engine changes (tenant policy translation), and a new lightweight telemetry probe + decision logic for safe quant adjustments. Key design points: 1) Jittered batcher: each tenant gets a small randomized offset window (configurable, deterministic for deduplication) to avoid synchronized microbursts across tenants while preserving max batch fill for throughput. 2) Adaptive quant scaler: takes tenant-level recent unit-econ and p95/p75 latency signals and proposes quant nudges (int8->int4 or FP16 variants) constrained by an SLA-derived safety budget and a quality gate using recent evals/held-out prompts. Changes are opt-in via tenant defaults; safe fallbacks route to tenant baseline model when probes fail. Checklist: - [x] Implement jitter offset generator and integrate into batch planner - [x] Add tenant policy schema to console and defaults service - [x] Telemetry probe and rollout circuit-breaker - [x] Decision engine with conservative ramp schedule and rollback hooks - [x] Unit tests for scheduler heuristics - [x] Integration tests for rollback/fallback behavior Rollout plan: feature gated behind tenant opt-in flag; staged rollout starting with internal test tenants, then low-traffic customers, followed by a two-week shadow run with telemetry-only mode. If regressions detected (latency p95 up > 10% or quality drift flagged), scaler automatically reverts to baseline and triggers an incident annotation. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged for tenants that do not opt in. New policy fields are additive and validated by the defaults service. Security/privacy: no customer payloads leave the cluster for probing; quality gate uses cached evaluation sets only. Risks and mitigations: risk of over-quantization hurting hallucination rates -> mitigation: quality gate rejects changes with token-level divergence above threshold and forces manual review; risk of jitter causing micro-latency variance -> mitigation: jitter magnitude bounded and throttled under high-latency conditions. Related: referenced ENG-1984 (tenant batch fairness) and ENG-2010 (unit-econ autosuggest).

review_comments: Rafael J. Ortega: Nice isolation approach. Two asks: (1) ensure jitter window is bounded by per-tenant latency SLO and (2) add a metric for 'jitter-induced fill-loss' so we can detect when offsets harm throughput.
Author (Maya): Added bound check against tenant.slo.ms and instrumented a new prometheus metric runtime_batch_jitter_fill_loss_total in the telemetry probe. See latest commit f1b8c55.
Priya Sinha: For the quant scaler, can you add a deterministic dry-run mode that emits proposed changes to the audit log without applying? We'll want to run this across a few tenants first.
Author (Maya): Added dry-run flag and audit log emitter (ops/telemetry/audit_emitter.go) in commit f1b8c55; dry-run enabled during shadow stage in rollout plan.
Daniel H. Lee: Integration tests look solid. One small nit: make the rollback delay configurable; sometimes we want faster reverts for critical tenants.
Author (Maya): Exposed rollback.delay_ms in tenant policy and defaults; updated console handler to surface it.
release_notes: Add tenant-jitter-batcher and an adaptive quant scaler with safety budgets. Opt-in feature; provides reduced tenant batch contention, improved unit-econ tuning with safe rollbacks and audit logging. See console for tenant policy fields and rollout options.
